sentences.text: Barbosania was a medium-sized pterodactyloid, a group of flying reptiles, that lived in northeastern Brazil. Its skull measured 392 millimeters in length and featured an elongated shape with a slight upward curve in the snout.
The total body length of this animal was 209.5 millimeters. Unlike some related pterosaurs, Barbosania lacks a rostral and dentary median sagittal crest on its skull.
It possesses thirteen dorsal vertebrae, a unique trait distinguishing it from the normal twelve found in related species.
The first four pairs of teeth in Barbosania are extremely long, forming a rosette adapted for catching slippery prey like fish or squids.
The holotype — the specimen the species is based on — consists of an almost complete, partially articulated, and uncompressed skeleton including the skull.

The genus Barbosania was named and described by Ross A. Elgin and Eberhard Frey in 2011. The generic name honors Professor Miguel Barbosa of the Museu de História Natural de Sintra, whose collection holds the type specimen.
The holotype specimen was prepared at the Staatliches Museum für Naturkunde Karlsruhe in Germany.
Researchers suggest that several specimens previously assigned to Brasileodactylus might actually belong to Barbosania.

Barbosania was originally assigned to the superfamily Ornithocheiroidea and the family Ornithocheiridae. In 2019, Pêgas et al. reclassified Barbosania into the clade Targaryendraconia and the family Targaryendraconidae.
Fossil evidence places Barbosania in existence between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago within the Aptian to Albian stages of the Romualdo Formation.
